headline: Clinton order directs the federal government to identify top trade priorities and foreign government buying practices that unfairly shut out US products.
what_it_does: Based on its title, this order calls for the federal government, likely through the US Trade Representative, to identify priority areas for opening foreign markets to US exports. It also calls for identifying foreign governments whose purchasing rules unfairly favor their own companies over US sellers. No summary was provided, so the specific steps, deadlines, and possible follow-up actions are not described here.

who_it_affects.group: US exporters and companies that sell to foreign governments
who_it_affects.how: Their complaints about blocked markets or unfair foreign government purchasing may be reviewed and listed as priorities for US trade action.
Their trade barriers and government purchasing practices may be formally named by the United States, which could lead to negotiations or other trade steps.
